cards.line: no judge's warrant, no need to open the door
cards.scene: a woman in her thirties stands two steps back from her own front door at night, completely still, arms down at her sides, deliberately not reaching for the handle. she is looking straight at the door, jaw set, frightened but holding. through the frosted glass panel in the upper half of the door, the dark shapes of two figures stand waiting on the other side. one bare hallway bulb lights the side of her face and the face of the door. everything else falls to near black.
cards.text_in: the sentence is carved into the painted wood of the door itself, gouged in with a blade, each stroke cut clean through the paint layer into the bare pale wood underneath. every groove holds dark shadow down one side and catches a bright edge of the hallway light down the other, so the letters read as real depth cut into the surface. the carving is imperfect and human: the depth wanders, some strokes are crooked or doubled where the blade slipped, paint is chipped and flaked back along the edges of every cut, and splinters stand up where the blade tore across the grain. it looks cut there years ago
cards.surface: the painted face of the front door

cards.line: the government will never call you for money
cards.scene: a small kitchen at night, one warm bulb. a phone lies face up on a formica counter, screen lit pale with an unknown number calling. a cold half drunk cup of tea beside it. beside them a thick cream government envelope lies flat and unopened.
cards.text_in: the sentence is pressed blind into the thick cream paper of that envelope, no ink at all, only the raised and sunken shapes of the letters catching a low raking light across the paper
cards.surface: the front of the cream government envelope

cards.line: the flight home is what triggers the ban
cards.scene: an empty airport departure gate at dawn, long rows of seats, one suitcase standing alone, a tall window with a plane waiting on the wet apron beyond, cold grey blue light flooding in.
cards.text_in: the sentence is engraved into the concrete floor itself, in the wide empty foreground, each letter a shallow trough cut into the slab. the insides of the grooves are darkened with years of grime and their top edges are worn pale and smooth by feet. every groove holds shadow on the side away from the window and catches the low dawn light on the side facing it, so the letters read as cut depth and not as paint. the cutting is imperfect, edges chipped, a few letters shallower than the rest, hairline cracks running off some strokes. it lies flat across the floor facing the camera on two stacked lines, well inside the frame with clear space at both edges
cards.surface: the painted concrete floor of the gate area

cards.line: none of this was hidden. nobody told you.
cards.scene: a woman in her thirties sits on the floor of a narrow hallway at night, her back against the wall, knees drawn up, one opened letter loose in her hand and four or five more envelopes fanned on the floorboards around her. she is looking down at the letter, tired, her face clearly visible and lit. the hallway is cold teal and nearly black. one warm amber light falls out of an open doorway behind her and lays a long panel of light across the floorboards in front of her.
cards.text_in: the sentence is carved into the wooden floorboards, hacked in roughly with a knife, the strokes cutting across the grain and straight through the varnish into raw pale wood. the grooves are uneven in depth and width, some strokes doubled where the blade slipped, torn grain and small splinters along every edge, the varnish chipped back around them. shadow sits in the bottom of each cut and the warm light from the doorway catches the raised edge of every stroke
cards.surface: the wooden floorboards inside the panel of light
